full_judgment:
10. Leave was granted to consider the following points such as (1) Whether serious question of disputed facts having being involved in the matter, the High Court Division erred in law in making the Rule absolute; (II) Whether the writ petitioner having not acquired any legal right under the special statutory jurisdiction, the High Court Division erred in law in making the Rule absolute; (III) Whether the order of direction against the rules laid down by the government in the interest of the whole nation, the High Court Division erred in law in making the Rule absolute and thus the impugned judgment and order is liable to be set as. 

 11. Mr. Sk. Md. Murshed, the learned Additional Attorney General on behalf of the appellants took us through the judgment and order dated 11.08.2010 of the High Court Division, the materials on record and submitted that the writ petitioner-respondent No.1 having not acquired any legal right under the special statutory jurisdiction, the High Court Division committed error of law in making the Rule absolute in part. The learned Counsel has contended further that the High Court Division failed to appreciate that BIWTA has no jurisdiction to allow the excavation of sand or soil from the Meghna River-bed rather the government through concerned Deputy Commissioner is the competent authority to allow the writ petitioner to extract sand or soil from any riverbed. The learned Counsel has submitted lastly that the High Court Division failed to appreciate that there is no provision for allowing any one to extract sand from the riverbed by the BIWTA. The High Court Division has committed illegality asking the respondent No.4 to dispose of the application as per recommendation of the respondent No.1, therefore, the impugned judgment and order passed by the High Court Division is liable to be set aside. 

 15. To get the answer of this question we shall have to go in the root of establishment of the Inland Water Transport Authority. The Inland Water Transport Authority was established as far back as in the year 1958 during Pakistan Government, vide Ordinance No.LXXV of 1958. Subsequently by an amendment in the year 1977 vide Ordinance No.LV of 1977 the Inland Water Transport Authority has been renamed as Bangladesh Inland Water Transport Authority (BIWTA). 

 17. To run the day to day functions and works of the authority, a fund namely 'Authority Fund' was created under the provision of Section 19 of the Inland Water Transport Authority Ordinance, 1958 which runs as follows: 

 (c)  (cc) The Government may empower the Authority to realise any or all of the tolls, taxes or fees specified in clause(c) of this sub-section. 

 (d) sale-proceeds of bonds issued under the authority of the Government; 

 (e) loans or grants obtained by the Authority with the special or general sanction of the Government; 

 (f) foreign aid and loans obtained from the Development Loan Fund or the International Bank of Reconstruction and Development or otherwise, with the sanction of, and on such terms and conditions as may be approved by the Government; and 

 (3) The Government may levy tolls, taxes, fees or charges in respect of all or any of the items, as specified in clause (c) of sub-section (2), at such rate and in such manner as are and/or as may be prescribed." 

 19. In sub-section (cc) it has been mentioned that "The Government may empower the Authority to realise any or all of the tolls, taxes or fees specified in clause (c) of this sub-section." But it appears from the provision mentioned in section 19(2)(c) that the authority did not have any power to allow any party or person to excavate sand or collect sand and sale it in the name of navigation of the river-bed. In Sub-section 3 of Section 19 it has been mentioned that "The Government may levy tolls, taxes, fees or charges in respect of all or any of the items, as specified in clause (c) of sub-section (2), at such rate and in such manner as are and/or as may be prescribed." 

 20. From the above it is abundantly clear that the authority i.e. BIWTA did not have any power to allow the writ petitioner to excavate and to collect sand from the river-bed of Meghna. Whatever the power is given to BIWTA by the aforesaid Ordinance it is subject to approval of the government. In this case it appears that the government i.e. the Deputy Commissioner, Chandpur did not give any approval to the BIWTA to permit the writ petitioner to extract or collect sand from the river-bed Meghna and to sell it to the market. 

 21. To manage the sand quarry and to conduct soil management, in the year 2010 government has enacted a law which is numbered as Act No.62 of 2010. The nomenclature of the said act is 'বালুমহাল ও মাটি ব্যবস্থাপনা আইন, ২০১০’। In the preamble of the said Act it has been stated that- “বালুমহাল ইজারা প্রদান ও আনুষঙ্গিক অন্যান্য বিষয়ে বিধান প্রণয়নকল্লে প্রণীত আইন। 

 23. This Act came into force on the 20th December, 2010. In the said Act there are provisions how to manage the sand quarries and soil excavation by the government. However, the judgment was pronounced by the High Court Division in Writ Petition No.3289 of 20009 on 11.08.2010 before enactment of the said Act, thus this law shall not be applicable in the present case. But before the new law of 2010 (Act 62 of 2010) was enacted there was another law namely "খনি ও খনিজ সম্পদ (নিয়ন্ত্রণ ও উন্নয়ন) আইন, ১৯৯২”, by which the sand quarries, stone quarries and the use of other minerals were con-trolled. Sub-section 2(Ka) of the said 'c511*9-, has defined about the 'Inquiry and Search License' which runs as fol-lows: 

 25. Section 3 of the said Act prohibits everybody from inquiring or searching any place other than by the licensee who got the license from the government in this regard. So it is also clear from the law i.e. খনি ও খনিজ সম্পদ (নিয়ন্ত্রণ ও উন্নয়ন) আইন, ১৯৯২, that, other than the government no authority like BIWTA had/has any power to allow the writ petitioner to extract or collect the sand from the Meghna River-bed and to sale it to the market. 

 26. The BIWTA assuming the power and jurisdiction of the government conferred by a specific law or statute cannot allow the writ petitioner to collect sand or extract sand from the river-bed of Meghna, at the same time it can be presumed that the respondent No.1, the Shipping Ministry was swayeded by the decision of BIWTA. The direction given by the High Court Division is also not proper because it hints the government to allow the writ petitioner to extract sand from the river-bed of Meghna. 

 27. From the impugned judgment it transpires that the High Court Division with-out taking consideration of the provision of BIWTA Act, 1958 and the খনি ও খনিজ সম্পদ (নিয়ন্ত্রণ ও উন্নয়ন) আইন, ১৯৯২, (Ain 39 of 1992) straightway treated the Meghna Riverbed within the approach channel of Chandpur-Shariatpur Ferry Service as 'Balumahal' and directed the writ respondent No.4 to dispose of the application of writ petitioner allowing the writ petitioner to extract sand from the Meghna River-bed on the basis of the instruction of writ respondent No.1 who is the controlling Ministry of BIWTA. 

 28. The High Court Division ignoring the Ain, 39 of 1992 and BIWTA Act, 1958 most illegally and arbitrarily directed to dispose of the writ petitioner's application as per instruction of the writ respondent No.1 facilitating the extraction of sand from the Meghna River-bed by the writ petitioner-respondent. 

 36. It also surprises us that on behalf of the government no affidavit-in-opposition was filed before the High Court Division to contest the Rule. The concerned government officials of Chandpur District administration slept over the matter for a long span of time. We express our dissatisfaction with the conduct of the concerned Government Officials of Chandpur District Administration, who did not take any initiative for years together to get the Rule heard.
